pr.title: Offer made-up syllables in memorable passwords with --syllables
pr.head: c65fc6a0b2bb4a7079caf8f8842ae81cbb13d180

summary: multipass can make new passwords with generate and add --generate, added in the layer beneath this one. One kind is the memorable password: several words from the EFF's large list of 7,776 words, joined by a separator, such as oxidize-tattered-flier-rebound-anyone.

1Password's memorable passwords can use short made-up syllables instead of real words. This layer adds that as --syllables, an option of --words. Each word becomes three letters: a consonant, a vowel, and a consonant, such as fip-wol-ruk-tes-bam. Separators and --capitalize work as they do for words.

A syllable is weaker than a word. There are 20 × 5 × 20 = 2,000 syllables, worth 11.0 bits each, against 12.9 bits for a word, so the default count of 5 gives 54.8 bits and the weak-password warning, and 6 syllables give 65.8 bits. The README advises about 1.2 syllables for each word you would have used. The strength line on stderr counts the units as syllables.
Whether to offer syllables at all is still an open question in the plan, waiting on the owner. The layer is one commit, so it can be dropped whole if the answer is full words only.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Recipe: the kind of password and its settings, built from the options. It holds no secret, so its strength can be printed.
  • Bits: the base-2 logarithm of how many passwords a recipe can make, each equally likely.
  • below(n): draws an index from 0 to n − 1 with no bias, by drawing again when a random 16-bit value would favor some indexes.
  • pick: reads one entry of a table by scanning every entry with a mask, so which memory is read does not depend on the secret index.

groups.title: Drawing a syllable
groups.kicker: The syllable alphabet, the draw, and the strength count in the crypto module
intro: src/crypto/generate.rs turns random bytes into a password. A memorable recipe's Words now carries a list, either WordList::Eff or WordList::Syllables, and the drawing loop branches on it. That branch is on the recipe, which is public, so it reveals nothing about the password.

For a syllable, the loop draws each of the three letters with the same below and pick the rest of the generator uses, from CONSONANTS (20 letters, all but q) and VOWELS (5). It writes them into the same nine-byte slot a word uses, with a fixed length of 3, so the step that squeezes out padding works unchanged.
The strength uses word_count(list), which for syllables is computed from the two tables. Nothing filters out real or offensive syllables, so every one of the 2,000 is possible and the count is exact.

files.note: Adds the letter tables and WordList, draws a syllable in draw_words, and counts syllables in word_count and entropy. One new test checks the syllable shape and that nearly all 2,000 syllables turn up.

checks.text: Each letter goes through below, the rejection draw, and pick, the masked read, so there is no % n and no table lookup indexed by the secret. Checked by reading, and against the AGENTS.md exception for the redraw decision.

20 × 5 × 20 = 2,000 syllables, and each is a distinct fixed-width string, so log2(2000) per syllable is exact. Hand-computed figures matched the release build: 68.4 bits for 6 syllables with --capitalize one, 76.4 bits for 5 with digit-or-symbol.

groups.title: The --syllables option
groups.kicker: Parsing the flag, building the recipe, and naming the unit in the strength line
intro: src/main.rs parses --syllables as a flag that takes no value and lists it in the help under --words. src/generator.rs holds it in Options, counts it among the options that need --words, sets the recipe's list from it, and prints syllables instead of words in the strength line.

Because it is one of the word options, --syllables alone or with --pin fails with --syllables needs --words, and on any command but generate and add --generate it fails as the other password options do.

checks.text: Driven against a release build with a temporary store: add site.example --generate --words 6 --syllables --capitalize one printed only the strength line, and get returned a six-syllable password with one capital. --syllables=yes, --syllables without --words, and add x --syllables each failed with a message.

files.note: Adds the syllables option, picks the list in words_recipe, and names the unit in strength. Tests pin the 6-syllable strength line and the error without --words.

checks.text: Listing --syllables in word_flags is what makes it an error without --words.

files.note: Parses --syllables, refuses an inline value, and adds it to the help text.

groups.title: README and plan
groups.kicker: Describing the option for users and in the plan
intro: The README's option table gains a --syllables row with an example and the strength per syllable. The plan's option row gains the same example and says the strength line counts the units as syllables.

files.note: Adds the --syllables row to the option table, with an example and how many syllables match a word count.

checks.text: "About 1.2 syllables for each word" holds at every count: a word is worth 1.18 syllables, so rounding 1.2 times the word count up always reaches the words' strength. Checked by computing every count from 3 to 15; the examples hold, 6 syllables at 65.8 bits against 64.6 for 5 words, and 12 at 131.6 against 129.2 for 10.

files.note: The plan's --syllables row (§ 2.2) now gives an example and the strength-line unit. The plan is still draft, and § 6 keeps syllables as an open question.
